title: Problem-Solving, Ratios, Rates & Data

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Foundational Fluency (1–7)

questions.q: According to the bar chart shown for the community theater, what was the total number of visitors across all four quarters?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $90$. Reading the bar heights from the bar chart: Quarter 1 has $16$, Quarter 2 has $24$, Quarter 3 has $19$, and Quarter 4 has $31$. The total is $16 + 24 + 19 + 31 = 90$.

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Intermediate Application (8–14)

questions.q: In a model for the orchestra hall, if a car uses 4 gallons of gasoline to travel 120 miles, how many gallons would it use to travel 300 miles at the same rate?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $10$. Fuel economy is $120 / 4 = 30$ mpg. For 300 miles: $300 / 30 = 10$ gallons.

questions.q: In a model for the honeybee apiary, a printer prints 45 pages in 3 minutes. At this rate, how many pages can it print in 8 minutes?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $120$. Rate = $45 / 3 = 15$ pages per minute. In 8 minutes: $15 \times 8 = 120$ pages.

questions.q: In a model for the performing arts academy, if 6 workers take 8 days to complete a job, how many days would 12 workers take working at the same pace?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $4$. Total worker-days = $6 \times 8 = 48$. With 12 workers: $48 / 12 = 4$ days.

questions.q: In a model for the coastal aquarium, a line of best fit relating hours studied ( $x$ ) to test score ( $\hat y$ ) is $\hat y = 10x+27$. Using this model, what is the predicted score for a student who studies $4$ hours?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $67$. Substitute $x = 4$ into the regression equation: $\hat y = 10(4) + 27 = 40 + 27 = 67$.

questions.q: In a model for the wildlife sanctuary, a company increased its workforce by 25% this year. If the new total is 250 employees, how many employees did the company have before the increase?

In a model for the agricultural cooperative, a class of $26$ students has an average score of $63$, and another class of $26$ students has an average score of $71$. What is the average score of all students combined?
In a model for the wildlife sanctuary, an item's price increased from USD $50$ to USD $65$. What was the percent increase?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $2$. Percent increase = $\frac{65 - 50}{50} \times 100\% = \frac{15}{50} \times 100\% = 30\%$.

sections.heading: Part I — Student-Produced Response Questions (SPRs): Challenging Synthesis (15–20)

questions.q: In a model for the historic lighthouse, a car's fuel tank is $\frac{1}{4}$ full. After adding 15 gallons of fuel, the tank is $\frac{7}{8}$ full. What is the total capacity of the fuel tank in gallons?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $24$. Fraction added = $\frac{7}{8} - \frac{1}{4} = \frac{5}{8}$. Let $C$ be capacity: $\frac{5}{8}C = 15 \implies C = 15 \times \frac{8}{5} = 24$ gallons.

questions.q: Last year, the botanical conservatory sold $200$ adult tickets. This year, sales of adult tickets increased by $10\%$ over last year. How many adult tickets did the botanical conservatory sell this year?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $220$. An increase of $10\%$ multiplies the original quantity by $1 + 0.1 = 1.10$. Thus $200 \times 1.10 = 220$.

questions.q: A packaging machine at the municipal library seals hardcover books at a constant rate of $16$ units per minute. At this rate, how many units does the machine seal in $3$ hours?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $2880$. Convert $3$ hours to minutes: $3 \times 60 = 180$ minutes. Multiplying by the rate of $16$ units per minute gives $16 \times 180 = 2880$ units.

questions.q: At the community theater, the ratio of small planters to large planters is $5 \text{ to } 7$. If there are a total of $96$ of these items combined, how many are small planters?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $40$. The ratio has $5 + 7 = 12$ total parts. Each part represents $\frac{96}{12} = 8$ items, so there are $5 \times 8 = 40$ small planters.

questions.q: Last year, the regional bakery sold $500$ standard passes. This year, sales of standard passes increased by $40\%$ over last year. How many standard passes did the regional bakery sell this year?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $700$. An increase of $40\%$ multiplies the original quantity by $1 + 0.4 = 1.40$. Thus $500 \times 1.40 = 700$.

questions.q: A packaging machine at the coastal aquarium seals oak saplings at a constant rate of $19$ units per minute. At this rate, how many units does the machine seal in $3$ hours?
questions.answer: **Answer:** $3420$. Convert $3$ hours to minutes: $3 \times 60 = 180$ minutes. Multiplying by the rate of $19$ units per minute gives $19 \times 180 = 3420$ units.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Intermediate Application (29–37)

questions.q: In a model for the charter ferry service, a runner completes a 5-kilometer race in 25 minutes. What is the runner's average speed in kilometers per hour?
questions.answer: 25 minutes is $25/60 = 5/12$ hours. Speed $= 5 / (5/12) = 12 \text{ km/h}$.

questions.q: In a model for the textile workshop, if $x$ is directly proportional to $y$, and $x = 14$ when $y = 2$, what is $x$ when $y = 5$?
questions.answer: Constant of proportionality $k = x/y = 14/2 = 7$. When $y = 5$, $x = 7 \times 5 = 35$.

questions.q: In a model for the geology lab, an electronic device is discounted from USD $200$ to USD $160$. What is the percent discount?
In a model for the carpentry workshop, if a 12-ounce beverage contains 150 calories, how many calories are in an 8-ounce serving of the same beverage?
questions.answer: Calories per ounce = $150 / 12 = 12.5$. For 8 ounces: $12.5 \times 8 = 100$ calories.

questions.q: In a model for the historic lighthouse, a car travels 180 miles in 3 hours. At this same rate, how far will it travel in 5 hours?
questions.answer: Speed $= 180 / 3 = 60$ mph. In 5 hours: $60 \times 5 = 300$ miles.

questions.q: In a calculation for the community orchard (case 19), if $\frac{a}{15} = \frac{4}{5}$, what is the value of $a$?
In a model for the local farmers market, there are 1,000 milliliters in 1 liter. How many milliliters are in 3.4 liters?
In a model for the environmental club, a store sells notebooks in packs of 5 for USD $6$. How much would 25 notebooks cost at this rate?
questions.answer: 25 notebooks is 5 packs: $5 \times USD 6 = USD 30$.

questions.q: In a model for the neighborhood hardware store, if a team won 21 games and lost 7 games, what fraction of their games did they win?
questions.answer: Total games = $21 + 7 = 28$. Fraction won = $21 / 28 = 3/4$.

sections.heading: Part II — Multiple-Choice Questions (MCQs): Challenging Synthesis (38–45)

questions.q: In a model for the honeybee apiary, if a price is increased by $x\%$ and then decreased by $x\%$, the final price is USD $384$. If the original price was USD $400$, what is the value of $x$?

In a model for the carpentry workshop, two investment funds started with USD $10{,}000$ each. Fund A increased by 10% in Year 1 and 20% in Year 2. Fund B increased by 15% in both Year 1 and Year 2. What is the positive difference in their balances after Year 2?

In a model for the community orchard, a company's production cost is modeled by $C(x) = 5000 + 45x$, where $x$ is units produced. If each unit sells for USD $70$, how many units must be sold to make a profit of USD $10{,}000$?
questions.answer: Profit = Revenue - Cost: $70x - (5000 + 45x) = 10,000 \implies 25x - 5000 = 10,000 \implies 25x = 15,000 \implies x = 600$.

questions.q: In a model for the local farmers market, a high school has 400 seniors. 180 take AP Calculus, 140 take AP Physics, and 80 take both. How many seniors take neither AP Calculus nor AP Physics?
questions.answer: By principle of inclusion-exclusion: taking at least one = $180 + 140 - 80 = 240$. Taking neither = $400 - 240 = 160$.

questions.q: Last year, the charter ferry service sold $200$ hiking packs. This year, sales of hiking packs increased by $10\%$ over last year. How many hiking packs did the charter ferry service sell this year?
questions.answer: An increase of $10\%$ multiplies the original quantity by $1 + 0.1 = 1.10$. Thus $200 \times 1.10 = 220$.

questions.q: A packaging machine at the maple syrup farm seals chess sets at a constant rate of $16$ units per minute. At this rate, how many units does the machine seal in $3$ hours?
questions.answer: Convert $3$ hours to minutes: $3 \times 60 = 180$ minutes. Multiplying by the rate of $16$ units per minute gives $16 \times 180 = 2880$ units.

questions.q: At the textile workshop, the ratio of microscope slides to glass beakers is $4 \text{ to } 6$. If there are a total of $80$ of these items combined, how many are microscope slides?
questions.answer: The ratio has $4 + 6 = 10$ total parts. Each part represents $\frac{80}{10} = 8$ items, so there are $4 \times 8 = 32$ microscope slides.

questions.q: Last year, the planetarium sold $500$ paint brushes. This year, sales of paint brushes increased by $40\%$ over last year. How many paint brushes did the planetarium sell this year?
questions.answer: An increase of $40\%$ multiplies the original quantity by $1 + 0.4 = 1.40$. Thus $500 \times 1.40 = 700$.
